- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts often peak too early or too high, then gradually decline — suggesting overshoot followed by mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices during sustained upward trends (e.g., 70–75 range) and overestimates during sharp declines.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window; later days show better alignment with true values.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — underestimates when prices are falling sharply.
- Forecasts are generally too optimistic in the middle of the 30-day window, especially when true values show consolidation or minor corrections.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon — often underestimates sharp drops or overestimates stability.
- When true values show strong mean reversion (e.g., from 75+ to 70–72), model forecasts remain elevated longer than warranted.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates volatility spikes and overestimates calm periods.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30-day history includes recent price consolidation or low volatility — less accurate when history shows sharp, sustained moves.
